title: 1:1 prep - ship risk & ops unblock (Zara)
content:
Meeting: 1:1 with Ari (eng lead - serving runtime)
Date/time: Mon 2026-03-15 10:30am PT (30m) — quick sync before team standup
Location: Zoom / quick notes in doc
Goals for this 1:1 (top 3, explicit asks)
1) Unblock Dedicated pilot for ACME: need explicit approval for +1 reserved GPU node for canary (explain why and timeframe). Ask: can Ari greenlight temporary reservation or point to owner?
2) Triage tail latency regression: get his view on top suspects (KV eviction, kernel selection change, batching policy). Ask: prioritize a production canary of KV-cache-tuned build this week.
3) Console rollout timing: confirm we can toggle new rollout UI with safe fallback; ask for an ETA on the feature flag and who owns the rollback hook.
Quick context (one-paragraph summary I can read aloud)
- ACME pilot is scheduled to start next Tue. Platform telemetry shows increased 99th tail for high-concurrency requests after the last runtime kernel update. Dedicated provisioning currently meets baseline but we expect spikes during ACME synthetic loads. The Console rollout includes new rollout UI for pinning model variants; we want the toggle and fallback path before pilot launch.
Key signals / metrics to call out (short bullets)
- 99th latency (text-gen route) last 48h: median ~120ms, p95 ~310ms, p99 ~620ms (target p99 <= 450ms)
- Token throughput per GPU down ~12% vs baseline on model-x-quant-8 (observed in nightly stress)
- KV cache miss ratio spike from 8% to 18% under mixed-concurrency tests
- Dedicated pool utilization target for ACME: 6 GPUs steady, need +1 burst capacity for canary (7 total)
Hypothesis / likely root causes (short list so Ari can react)
- Kernel selector change: new heuristic picks a slower kernel for short sequences at high concurrency.
- Batching policy: queue time growth with greedy batching when many small requests arrive together.
- KV cache eviction: default cache size not tuned for ACME prompt mix -> more recompute and latency spikes.
What I want from Ari in this meeting (concrete asks)
- Quick verdict on whether we can reserve +1 GPU node for ACME canary through Friday (owner + cost impact).
- Prioritize a KV-cache-tuned canary build to run on dedicated pool by Wed; assign eng owner and testing plan.
- Confirm the rollout UI feature flag will include automatic fallback to legacy behavior and name the rollback owner.
- If he thinks the kernel selector is suspect, ask his recommended revert cadence and who owns that PR.
Potential pushback I should anticipate and responses (prep lines)
- "Budget constraints for extra GPU" -> response: short-term +1 is covered by pilot budget; tradeoff is lower risk of public incident and faster go/no-go. Will sunset after pilot.
- "Not enough test coverage for KV change" -> response: we can run targeted synthetic load tests against the dedicated canary pool before customer traffic.
- "Rollout UI not ready" -> response: need a fallback plan: console allowed to opt into new UI per-tenant, default to old UI until flagged. Require rollback owner and a test flip.
Notes to self / talking points (bullet-y, quick)
- Start with status (1 min): metrics + ACME timeline.
- Ask for short commitments (owners + day) not vague promises.
- If Ari pushes for more investigation time, request a measurable gate (e.g., hold pilot if p99 > 550ms under synthetic).
- Request adding infra alert to track KV miss ratio crossing 12% during pilot.
Follow-ups (action list I will send after meeting)
- If +1 GPU approved: create ticket INF-7233 and add cost owner (finance cc), set expiry date (2026-04-01). Owner: me (Zara) to create, Ari to approve.
- KV canary: create a canary run doc with test plan + acceptance criteria (p99 <= 450ms under synthetic load) — Owner: Ethan (eng) to execute, duplicate to me. Due: Wed 2026-03-17 EOD.
- Rollout UI: get feature-flag config and name rollback owner + test flip window. Owner: Rina (product infra) to coordinate. Due: Thu 2026-03-18.
- Add alert: KV-miss-ratio > 12% -> paging to eng oncall (SRE). Owner: Ari to assign. Due: Tue 2026-03-16.
Open questions I want Ari to answer live
- Which kernel selector PR changed the short-seq heuristic? Visible in GH: PR #458 — is a revert on the table?
- Can we get a schedule for the canary regression run (timeslot, GPUs reserved)?
- Does Dedicated autoscaler support temporary hard-reserve of +1 for 48h? If not, what's the workaround?
Pre-reads I attached in the Slack thread (good to reference quickly)
- stress-run-2026-03-09.csv (nightly metrics)
- kv-cache-analysis-notes (internal gist)
- PR #458 summary + perf table
Things I should not ask / avoid in meeting
- Do not ask Ari to commit to long-term architecture changes in 1:1; focus on immediate unblock and owners.
- Avoid deep dive into Console UI UX decisions — poke product leads instead, keep the ask to feature-flag/rollback mechanics.
Post-meeting template (what I'll send as follow-up)
- 1-line status + ask results (approved/denied/needs more info)
- Action items list: owner + due date + link to ticket/pr
- Short risks / fallback if items not done by due date
Personal notes to track next 2 meetings (for continuity)
- Check infra ticket progress: INF-7233 status + cost approvals.
- Validate canary results (metrics snapshot + test environment tag).
- Confirm rollout UI feature-flag test flip completed and rollback validated.
Random sticky ideas / brainstorm (notes-to-self)
- Could we add a temporary KV cache boost for tenants in pilot mode? Maybe a per-tenant cache multiplier behind flag.
- Consider a short-lived "pilot mode" orchestration that increases batching aggressiveness threshold to avoid queue spikes.
- Add a simple dashboard for pilot tenants showing p95/p99, KV miss ratio, and reserved GPUs.
-- END --
summary: Prep doc for PM (Zara) to run a focused 1:1 with serving runtime lead. Covers metrics, asks, risks, and concrete follow-ups for Dedicated pilot and Console rollout.
